s: links two nouns, often a person and an activity, in rhetoric questions to express an opposition between them
Er und Abwaschen? Vielleicht einmal im Jahr!
Him doing the dishes? Maybe once per year!
und.et: From Middle High German unde, from Old High German unti, from Proto-Germanic *andi, *anþi, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énti. Compare Dutch en, English and, Danish end.
From Middle High German unde, from Old High German unti, from Proto-Germanic *andi, *anþi, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énti. Compare Dutch en, English and, Danish end.

s: et cetera, and so on, and so forth
something that is unheard of, unacceptable, and/or immoral
Unding.et: From Middle High German undinc, undinge, equivalent to un- + Ding (“thing”). Compare Dutch onding, West Frisian ûnding, English unthing.

s: introduces a clarification; namely, that is to say
Die Möglichkeit einer neuen, und zwar einer journalistischen Laufbahn, schien sich ihm zu eröffnen.
The possibility of a new, namely a journalistic career seemed to open up to him.

undankbar.et: From un- + dankbar or un- + Dank + -bar.

s: Das Opfer wurde erstickt und/oder erdrosselt.
The victim was choked and/or strangled.
AND gate, a logic gate performing a Boolean logic AND operation
et cetera; and so on; on and on; implying that the list is particularly long, and often that something is a burden
Für ihn Essen kochen, sein Bett machen, ihn umsorgen und, und, und.
Cooking his food, making his bed, caring for him, and so on.
Und dann: in der Sitzung nichts als Widerstände, eine miese Stimmung zum Zerschneiden, Parteiungen, Misstrauen und, und, und.
And then, there's nothing but resistance in the meeting, a miserable mood you cut cut with a knife, factions, mistrust, and so on.
underdog (competitor thought to be at disadvantage)
Als Underdog hat Otto Rehhagel, die vom Anstreicher zum Bohemien gewandelte Trainerlegende, seine spektakulärsten Erfolge gefeiert.
As an underdog, Otto Rehhagel, the house painter turned bohemian manager legend, celebrated his most spectacular successes.

Undank.et: From Middle High German undanc, from Old High German undank, undanc (“unthankfulness”), from Proto-West Germanic *unþank, from Proto-Germanic *unþankaz, equivalent to un- + Dank. Cognate with Dutch ondank, Old English unþanc ("unfavour, unpleasure, anger, ill-…

s: Der Arzt hat mir Pillen, Kapseln, Salben und was nicht alles verschrieben.
The doctor prescribed me pills, capsules, salves, and whatnot.
„Die Weigerung des Magistrats war durchaus undeutsch“, stellte Jadassohn fest. „Das nationale Banner muß hochgehalten werden“, verlangte Diederich.
anti-German; contrary to ideals of Germanness

Undankbarkeit.et: From undankbar + -keit; equivalent to un- + Dankbarkeit

s: good deeds for the sake of others are unlikely to be met with gratitude, but are nevertheless honorable
Undank ist der Welten Lohn.et: Literally, “ungratefulness is the reward of the world”. The form Welten, here, is not a plural but an archaic genitive singular. Compare Dutch ondank is 's werelds loon, Swedish otack är världens lön, Danish utak er de armes løn.

s: thorn (especially one worse than a typical thorn)

und wenn sie nicht gestorben sind, dann.i: /ʊnt ˈvɛn zi ˌnɪçt ɡəˈʃtɔʁbən zɪnt ˌdan ˈleːbən zi ˌnɔx ˈhɔʏ̯tə/
s: and they lived happily ever after (formulaic ending of fairy tales)
und wenn sie nicht gestorben sind, dann.et: Literally, “and if they haven’t died, they are still alive today”.

s: a little more than; and change
Und? Wie viele sind’s? — Hundert und ein paar Gequetschte.
So? How many are they? — A hundred and change.
und ein paar Gequetschte.et: Literally, “and some bruised ones”. Plausibly from such contexts as fruit harvesting, which yielded a certain saleable quantity plus some damaged ones for private consumption.

s: ellipsis of und so weiter (“and so on”)

Angela Merkel - die Facebook-Queen
Ja, klar. Sie ist Kanzlerin, mächtigste Frau der Welt und so.

Angela Merkel - Queen of Facebook
Yeah, sure. She's the chancellor, the world's most powerful woman and all.
